title: Debugging & Root-Cause Analysis
description: Study reproduce with minimal evidence, trace state and data flow, use logs and debuggers selectively, and verify the root cause and regression. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Reproduce with minimal evidence
lessons.description: Build a fixture with that record and explain the expected fallback.
lessons.conceptOverview: Create the smallest reliable reproduction that preserves the failure. Record inputs, environment and expected behavior so a fix can be checked without relying on memory.
lessons.whyItMatters: A stable reproduction anchors diagnosis and regression checking.

lessons.title: Trace state and data flow
lessons.description: Trace the unit through parsing, aggregation and rendering.
lessons.conceptOverview: Follow values from input through transformation to output. Identify where an invariant first breaks instead of patching the last visible symptom.
lessons.whyItMatters: Fix the earliest incorrect transformation that causes the symptom.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Follow values from input through transformation to output. Identify where an invariant first breaks instead of patching the last visible symptom.

lessons.title: Use logs and debuggers selectively
lessons.description: Add a correlation identifier and call-site evidence.
lessons.conceptOverview: Choose observations that distinguish hypotheses, such as variable values, call counts or timing spans. Excessive logging can obscure the failure and expose data without improving diagnosis.
lessons.whyItMatters: Diagnostic instrumentation should answer a specific question.

lessons.title: Verify the root cause and regression
lessons.description: Check data preservation as well as absence of the crash.
lessons.conceptOverview: A root-cause fix should make the original reproduction pass and preserve related behavior. If the symptom disappears only because an error is hidden, the cause may remain.
lessons.whyItMatters: Regression verification must test intended behavior, not merely silence.

keyTakeaways: Regression verification must test intended behavior, not merely silence.
commonMistakes: No visible exception proves the underlying bug is fixed.
